title: Design System: Next Gen Water Systems

ground.note: Painted on html, never on body: the fixed scene sits at z-index -1 between the two in paint order. Measured at #ffffff on 18 Sep 2026, and the hero's own WebGL set measures #ffffff with it.

panel.note: The ground of the quiet sections that alternate with white, plus the spec table, form fields, the footer, the booking tab track and the system panel. Measured at #f6f7f7.

panel-2.note: Wells, pressed surfaces, and the ground a path photograph sits on before it loads. Rare.

studio.note: A FALLBACK, not the studio. It is the CSS ground of the fixed stage layer, painted under the canvas and visible only while the canvas is faded out. The set you actually see is set-pool to set-corner.

set-pool.note: The journey backdrop at the centre of the pool of light, sampled from real pixels on 18 Sep 2026. Neutral by measurement: red equals green, blue two levels under. The scene's source stop is a linear #c8c8c6; this is what the Neutral tone mapper puts on screen.

set-corner.note: The same backdrop at the frame corners. Second Ink over this falls under 4.5:1, which is why journey copy takes full Cover Ink.

ink.note: Sampled from the cover's own lettering. Headings, journey body copy, row values, the booking tab's selected fill, the focus ring on a filled button, the top rule of a data table, every callout leader and mark ring. Journey copy measures 5.10:1 over the set, which is the system's floor.

ink-2.note: Leads, section prose, row copy, the quiet link and the quiet button at rest. About 10:1 on white. Never used over the set.

ink-3.note: Labels, captions, the note beside a figure, a stage number inside a tab title, a path dot before it lights, field placeholders. 5.2:1 on white.

hairline.note: Every rule, border and row divider, and the one-pixel ring that replaces a border on a 12px or 16px corner. Darkens to 0.26 on a tab hover and 0.32 on a tab chosen.

accent.note: Deliberately singular. One filled pill per surface, inline links, sequence counters, and every focus ring that is not on a filled button. About 6.1:1 on white. There is no blue-100, no blue border token and no second accent.

deep.note: The action's hover and focus fill. It has no other job.

water.note: Water itself: selection at 28% alpha, the live dot in the hint pill, the fill under a freshly ticked chip, the journey heading forming out of water. 2.7:1 on white and never a word.

redline.note: The honesty colour. The [PLACEHOLDER] mark, the form's error line, the 'Request logged' stamp. Never decoration, never a heading.

display.purpose: The hero line only, plus the booking headline and an interior sheet's title at their own clamps. Balanced wrap, two lines.

headline.purpose: Every section heading on every page. One ramp step for all of them; sections do not compete on size.

beat.purpose: The journey's copy beats, each word rising out of its own overflow-clipped line. The one bold headline tier.

title.purpose: A stage tab's name, a path step's title. Siblings: a package title at 21px, a figure note's heading at 17px, a question at 19px in 600.

lead.purpose: The one sentence under a headline, in Second Ink on a 42 to 44ch measure.

body.purpose: A journey beat's paragraph in full Cover Ink on 40ch, a question's answer on 62ch, interior-sheet prose at 1.72 on 66ch.

row.purpose: The value side of a hairline row, a package list item, a path step's paragraph. The tier that carries the commercial half of the page.

label.purpose: Caption heads and the key side of a hairline row, in Third Ink, sentence case. Tracking 0, or 0.02em on a table key and a chip; the journey rail is the one exception at 0.04em.

caption.purpose: Breadcrumbs, the note under a generated photograph, form field labels, the note beside an action, the nav hint.

action.purpose: The pill's label. Satoshi ships 400, 500 and 700, so 600 resolves to the Bold file. The nav pill is 14px.

shadows.name: ring
shadows.purpose: The border of a rounded panel, a package card, the booking tab track. Flat; it is a border, not a lift, and it shares the arc of a 12px or 16px corner in a way a 1px border does not.

shadows.name: action
shadows.purpose: Under the blue pill, tinted with the pill's own colour. The only coloured shadow in the system.

shadows.name: plate
shadows.purpose: A photograph presented as a plate (the kettle figure). The deepest shadow in the system.

shadows.name: tile-selected
shadows.purpose: A stage tab once chosen. The only case where a shadow marks state.

shadows.name: note
shadows.purpose: A note floating over a photographic plate.

shadows.name: tag
shadows.purpose: A callout tag over the WebGL set. The note's shape, lighter.

shadows.name: floating-card
shadows.purpose: The phone journey card at the base of the screen.

shadows.name: mark-ring
shadows.purpose: A numbered hotspot on a photograph. A 1.5px ink ring is how a mark reads on any ground.

shadows.name: dot-ring
shadows.purpose: A 10px callout dot on a part in the scene.

shadows.name: dot-ring-unlit
shadows.purpose: A numbered path dot before its step lights.

shadows.name: nav-seat
shadows.purpose: The header's one-pixel seat while it is attached at the top of the page.

shadows.name: nav-detached
shadows.purpose: The header once it has detached into a floating pill. Cross-faded against nav-seat by the scroll scalar.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The only easing curve in the system (--ease). Quick to leave, slow to land.

motion.name: colour
motion.purpose: A link or a glyph changing colour.

motion.name: fill
motion.purpose: A button changing fill, border or shadow. A hover is a fill change and nothing else.

motion.name: tile
motion.purpose: A stage tab's background, border and shadow settling into its chosen state.

motion.name: mark-in
motion.purpose: A numbered hotspot arriving from scale 0.6. An arrival, never a hover.

motion.name: note-in
motion.purpose: A note rising 10px into place beside a plate, and the phone action bar sliding up from translateY(160%).

motion.name: crossfade
motion.purpose: A stage photograph cross-fading in from scale 1.02.

motion.name: lit
motion.purpose: A path photograph coming up from 0.5 opacity and 0.6 saturation as its step lights.

motion.name: still
motion.purpose: The hero's rendered still fading out once WebGL is live.

motion.name: nav-morph
motion.purpose: Width, height, radius and inset are written every frame from the scroll scalar over 260px. Deliberately untransitioned: the scroll is the timeline, and a transition on top of it reintroduces the lag that read as rigid.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: display: none on .journey and .stage-fixed; transition: none on the stage and path photographs and the phone bar
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion the pinned journey and the whole scene are removed and a static story carries the same beats with a still per stage.

breakpoints.name: rail-clear
breakpoints.purpose: The journey rail moves up to clear the stage marker.

breakpoints.name: tel-glyph
breakpoints.purpose: The nav's phone number drops its digits and keeps its glyph.

breakpoints.name: cut
breakpoints.purpose: The cut. A shorter journey timeline for a narrow camera, every multi-column grid stacks, beats become cards, callouts go, the phone action bar appears.

breakpoints.name: landscape
breakpoints.purpose: The beat card stands beside the machine at min(46vw, 400px) and the rail moves to the top right.

breakpoints.name: burger
breakpoints.purpose: The nav links and the quick-menu button hide behind the burger; the kettle plate unsticks and its hotspots become a tappable key list.

breakpoints.name: lockup
breakpoints.purpose: The compact lockup shrinks to 15px and the taste question left-aligns.

components.name: Primary Action

components.html: Book your free water test

components.name: Quiet Link

components.description: One of three sticky tiles that drive the stage explorer's photograph. Shown at rest and chosen.
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: grid; gap: 10px; max-width: 360px; } .ds-tab { display: grid; gap: 5px; width: 100%; padding: 18px 20px 19px; border: 1px solid var(--hairline, rgba(23, 25, 28, 0.12)); border-radius: 12px; background: var(--ground, #fff); text-align: left; font: inherit; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), border-color 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), box-shadow 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-tab:hover { border-color: rgba(23, 25, 28, 0.26); } .ds-tab.is-on { background: var(--panel, #f6f7f7); border-color: rgba(23, 25, 28, 0.32); box-shadow: 0 18px 34px -26px rgba(23, 25, 28, 0.5); } .ds-tab:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #0b62b8); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-tab-name { font-family: var(--font-satoshi), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 19px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: -0.01em; color: var(--ink, #17191c); } .ds-tab-num { display: inline-block; min-width: 1.15em; margin-right: 0.35em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--ink-3, #676e75); } .ds-tab-in { font-family: var(--font-hanken), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14.5px; line-height: 1.45; color: var(--ink-3, #676e75); }

components.name: Booking Tabs
components.description: A centred pill track over the booking form. The one place a solid ink fill marks selection.
components.css: .ds-track { display: flex; width: max-content; padding: 4px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--panel, #f6f7f7); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--hairline, rgba(23, 25, 28, 0.12)); } .ds-track-tab { height: 38px; padding: 0 18px; border: 0; border-radius: 999px; background: transparent; font-family: var(--font-hanken), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14.5px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--ink-2, #3e4348); cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), color 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-track-tab.is-on { background: var(--ink, #17191c); color: #fff; } .ds-track-tab:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #0b62b8); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Package Card
components.description: The one rounded-panel family: a picture and its hairline-row list as a single object.
components.html:
The installation

  • Licensed plumber, half a day on site
  • Mounted at the mains, no power point
  • Certificate of compliance
components.css: .ds-pk { display: grid; grid-template-rows: auto auto 1fr; align-content: start; max-width: 380px; padding: 12px 12px 14px; border-radius: 16px; background: var(--ground, #fff); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--hairline, rgba(23, 25, 28, 0.12)); } .ds-pk-photo { margin: 0; border-radius: 10px; overflow: hidden; aspect-ratio: 16 / 7; } .ds-pk-photo img { display: block; width: 100%; height: 100%; object-fit: cover; } .ds-pk-t { margin: 18px 0 0; padding: 0 12px; font-family: var(--font-satoshi), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 21px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: -0.015em; color: var(--ink, #17191c); } .ds-pk-list { margin: 12px 0 0; padding: 0 12px; list-style: none; } .ds-pk-list li { padding: 9px 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--hairline, rgba(23, 25, 28, 0.12)); font-family: var(--font-hanken), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; line-height: 1.5; color: var(--ink-2, #3e4348); }

components.name: Hairline Row
components.description: The system's fact carrier: a solid ink top rule, keys left in Label, values right in Row with tabular figures.

components.name: Callout Tag
components.description: A dot on the part, a hairline leader and a paper tag, drawn as HTML over the WebGL canvas so the type stays crisp while the leader stays attached.

narrative.overview:
A product-photography studio with the page as its backdrop. The page is white. One WebGL scene is fixed behind the whole document, and the page opens two windows onto it: the hero, where the set is driven to white so the machine stands on the page itself, and the journey, where the set becomes a lit neutral-grey seamless backdrop with a pool of light in it. Every other section is an opaque sheet over that scene. The type is the charcoal of the cover's own lettering. There is one blue and it is spent on the action.

The register is premium restraint (PRODUCT.md): closer to an appliance launch than to a plumbing site. Density is low at the top of the page and rises as a visitor gets closer to buying. The hero and the journey give one idea a whole screen; the commercial half of the page (the stage explorer, the numbered path, the package panels, the questions, the booking tabs) is denser, because by then the visitor is comparing rather than being introduced. Motion belongs to the machine. The cover turns under a drag and lifts under a tap; each housing opens in section on the scroll; the chrome around it changes fill and nothing else.

Confirmed rejections, from the direction contract and PRODUCT.md: the blue water-splash hero, the three feature cards, the stats band and the testimonial carousel of the category; the drawing-set furniture of the world this page replaced (sheet strips, sheet numbers, registration ticks, tracked-out drafting labels); and the wellness aesthetic (sage, blush, rounded friendly type, droplets as decoration).
keyCharacteristics: White page, a lit grey set behind two windows, charcoal ink, one blue.
The product is live in the first viewport and is the only picture that matters.
Satoshi Medium for the big lines; Hanken for sentences and for every label, in sentence case.
Hairline rows for facts; a rounded panel only where a picture and its list are one object.
Flat paper: a shadow only where something floats over the page or over the set.
A visible red placeholder wherever a figure has no source.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Action Blue is spent on the action and on what leads to it: one filled pill per surface, inline links, the counters that index a sequence. It never tints a background, a heading or a decoration. Two filled blue pills on one screen means one of them is wrong. The blue is deliberately singular: there is no blue-100, no blue border token, no second accent.

rules.name: The Water Is Never Text Rule
rules.body: Carried over. Water marks water: a selection, a live dot, the fill under a live chip, a heading forming out of water. At 2.7:1 on white it is never a word.

rules.name: The Set Is Lit, The Page Is Not Rule
rules.body: The grey behind the machine is a gradient because it is a lit backdrop, and its falloff is produced by a shader, not by a CSS gradient. A gradient on the page itself is allowed in exactly two places, and both simulate a physical material rather than decorate: the nav's frosted pane (a 180-degree wash over a 16px backdrop blur) and the water-bead cursor (three radial gradients, a rim and one specular). No flat surface, no button and no heading carries a gradient fill, and no type sits on one except over the set, where it is placed on the pool of light and measured.

rules.name: The Machine Keeps Its Own Colours Rule
rules.body: The palette above is the page's. The machine is a manufactured object and carries the colours it is made in: a blue valve handle (#1f5fb0), blue cartridge caps (#2c48c9), a red gauge needle (#c8281e), brass, copper, stainless. Those live in materials.ts, they are not tokens, and they are not counted against the one-blue rule. Do not 'correct' them toward the palette.

rules.name: The Red Means Unsourced Rule
rules.body: A figure without a source is set as a red dashed [PLACEHOLDER] mark. It is never replaced with a plausible number and never softened to grey.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: Every measured text-on-background pair on the shipping surface clears 4.5:1, and the floor is the journey's body copy over the set at 5.10:1, with the stage chips at 6.34:1 or better and the footer credit at 9.3:1. Copy over the set takes full Cover Ink, never Second Ink, because Second Ink falls under the floor toward the frame corners.

rules.name: The Two Faces Rule
rules.body: Satoshi sets headings, titles and the action. Hanken sets everything else, every label and every number included. No third face appears on a text surface. Enforcement is by override rather than by absence: the build re-points --font-mono and --font-draft at Hanken, and names Hanken directly with !important on the label selectors the retired stylesheets used to set in a drafting face.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels and keys are sentence case. No uppercase, no tracked small caps, no monospace for keys or numbers. Tabular figures are the only numeric treatment.

rules.name: The Medium Weight Rule
rules.body: The bigger the line, the lighter the weight. Display and headline sit at 500 with tight tracking; 700 belongs to the title tier and to the journey beats; 600 to the action and to a control that reads as a heading.

rules.name: The Counter Is Not A Kicker Rule
rules.body: Numbers that index the product are allowed: three stages, four steps in the path, three marks on the kettle photograph. They sit inside the thing they number and count plainly, 1 2 3, with no leading zero. A number floating above a section as a 01 marker is furniture and is not used.

rules.name: The One Scene Rule
rules.body: The machine is one WebGL scene fixed behind the page. The hero and the journey are windows onto it and paint nothing; every other section is opaque, and an opaque section taller than a screen sits between the two windows so the scene changes hands unseen. A new section that lets the set show through is a bug.

rules.name: The Alternating Ground Rule
rules.body: Sections alternate Page White and Paper down the page. White carries the sections with a picture or a live object in them; Paper carries the sections that are mostly words. Two Paper sections must not touch.

rules.name: The Hairline Row Rule
rules.body: Carried over from the previous world's Hairline Rule. Facts go in rows: key on the left, value on the right, a hairline between rows, one solid Cover Ink rule at the top of a table. A rounded panel is used only when a picture and its list are one object, never to hold a fact on its own.

rules.name: The Floating Paper Rule
rules.body: Carried over from the previous world's Paper-and-Glass Rule. A shadow says the element is off the page. It says nothing about importance. Rows, tables, fields, tabs at rest and notes on the page are flat; the action, a floating card, a plate, a note over a plate, the phone bar and the chrome over the set cast one.

rules.name: The Ring Not Border Rule
rules.body: Anything with a 12px or 16px corner takes 0 0 0 1px var(--hairline) instead of a border, so the inner fill and the edge share the same arc and a photograph inside it can bleed to the corner.

dos: Do give every surface one filled pill in Action Blue and make its second action a quiet link or a hairline outline.
Do set the big line in Satoshi Medium (500) at -0.03em or tighter, wrapped to two lines with a hard break, with one Hanken sentence under it in Second Ink on a 42 to 44ch measure.
Do set labels and keys in Hanken 500 at 13.5px, sentence case, Third Ink, tracking 0 to 0.02em.
Do put facts in hairline rows with a solid ink top rule, key left and value right, tabular figures.
Do alternate Page White and Paper down the page, and paint an opaque ground on every new section so the set shows only through the hero and the journey.
Do measure copy that sits over the set, place it in the pool of light, and give it full Cover Ink; 5.10:1 is the floor the build holds.
Do give a rounded panel a one-pixel hairline ring instead of a border.
Do keep the machine live: the scene is the picture, and a raster stands in only until WebGL is up or when motion is reduced.

Do mark any unsourced figure with the red dashed [PLACEHOLDER], caption a generated image as a visualisation on the page it appears on, and add a row to public/photos/PROVENANCE.md for any raster that ships.
Do cut every still through the same lens chain the page uses, so a still never looks like a different camera.
Do keep the reduced-motion path whole: no pinned journey, no scene, the same story as a document with a still per stage.
Do leave the nav's four morph properties untransitioned; the scroll is the timeline and a transition on top of it reintroduces the lag.
donts: Don't introduce a third blue, a blue background or a blue border token; Action Blue fills the action and colours links, Deep Blue is its hover, Water marks water.
Don't set type in Water, or in Second Ink over the set; both fall under the floor.
Don't paint a gradient on a flat surface, a button or a heading. The set's falloff is a lit backdrop produced by a shader; the nav pane and the cursor are materials. Nothing else gets one.

Don't use a monospace or a drafting face on a text surface, tracked uppercase, sheet numbers, sheet strips or registration ticks; the drawing set is retired and the two face variables are re-pointed so it cannot come back.
Don't float a number above a section as an 01 marker. A counter belongs inside the thing it counts.
Don't put a scrim, a halo or a text shadow behind copy over the set; move the copy or step the camera aside.

Don't build a feature-card grid, a stats band or a testimonial carousel; the direction contract refuses the category's furniture. A rounded panel is for a picture and its list together, not for three parallel claims.
Don't drift toward wellness: no sage or blush, no rounded friendly type, no droplets or leaves as decoration.
Don't quote a reduction percentage or any figure without a source document; describe the mechanism instead, in the datasheet's own terms.

Don't let a hover state move anything. A hover is a fill change, a border darkening or a colour change. A press may compress (the quick-menu button at 0.94) and a mark may scale in as it arrives; neither is a hover.
Don't let a sticky column release over the next section; give it a runway inside its own.
Don't add to globals.css or brand.css. They are the retired world's stylesheets, kept only until they are pruned; new rules go in world.css or sections.css.
